title: A firm's production and credit line in the synthetic commercial-bank economy
description: One firm in the closed synthetic economy (worldmodel.coupled_economy) chooses a constant daily production quantity and credit line for 30 days. A household buys through lagged demand feedback; the policy rate follows a rule; the loan rate passes it through; quotes adjust to inventory. On day 10 unit costs and rate expectations shift. Every quantity is fictional; only two mechanisms carry estimated parameters, and one of those failed its holdout.

decision_maker.role: Owner-manager of the economy's only firm
decision_maker.description: Fictional. Its production and borrowing move its own cash, the household's cash and the bank's book; they do not move the policy rate.

production.description: Goods ordered from the worker each day; rationed by cash, credit, capacity and labor.

credit_limit.description: Credit line requested from bank a.

success_criteria.description: The firm never misses an interest payment (unpaid interest bankrupts it).
Deposits cover loan principal on day 30.

policy_rate_rule.description: Smoothed Taylor-type rule on daily inflation and output-gap inputs.

evidence.note: Fitted on quarterly first releases; fails beats_persistence_dm, so it has no demonstrated forecast edge over a random walk.

loan_rate_pass_through.description: Error-correction of the annual loan rate toward spread + pass_through * policy rate.

evidence.note: Prime rate on the federal funds rate, monthly; the estimate's per-month speed is carried to a daily step by the component's own conversion.

price_adjustment.description: Automatic quote from the inventory gap and lagged unmet demand.

evidence.note: price_adjustment.eia_monthly estimates adjustment = -0.0035, outside this mechanism's [0, 1] and failing parameters_within_declared_bounds; it cannot be bound.

demand_response.description: Household demand scaled by (reference/price)^elasticity and lagged rate expectations.

evidence.note: demand_price_elasticity.eia_monthly estimates elasticity = -0.124 (gasoline, wrong sign for this mechanism) and fails parameters_within_declared_bounds; it cannot be bound.

household_demand.description: Base daily purchase request before price and rate feedback.

inflation.description: Inflation input to the policy rule, every day.

output_gap.description: Output-gap input to the policy rule, every day.

expected_rate_change.description: Household rate expectation set on day 10; lowers demand the next day onward.

does_not_establish: The economy has one firm, one household and two banks; its money, goods and prices are fictional.
A rate estimated on monthly US prime and federal funds data is applied to a fictional daily loan; the transfer is itself an assumption.
